title: Rust tests are not portable to a fresh Windows host: 133 fail on a hard-coded "/tmp" workdir, 70 on path length (Windows B gate on 09d5875a)
outcome: Rust tests are not portable to a fresh Windows host: 133 fail on a hard-coded "/tmp" workdir, 70 on path length (Windows B gate on 09d5875a)
acceptance: Each of the 203 rust-tests failures in Windows B gate test-e725bb78 (on 09d5875a) is attributed to a recorded cause group with evidence: hard-coded '/tmp' workdir (133), 'Filename too long' / '$GIT_DIR too big' path-length failures (43 + up to 27), or another named cause.

Tests no longer depend on a host directory existing outside their own fixtures (for example '/tmp' resolving to <drive>:\tmp on Windows). They use the existing fixture temp facilities, without retries, skips or weakened assertions.

The 43 path-length failures and the 26 other failures that pass on the default temp are attributed, with Windows B r2 evidence (gate test-4bdb83a3 on 09d5875a), to that run's in-repository TERMAL_TEST_USER_TEMP placement, not to a product or fixture defect. They are resolved by running with the launcher's default tool-owned test temp, with no host or global Git configuration change. Supporting a long in-repository test temp on Windows, if needed, is tracked as its own item.
A full gate on Windows B with the launcher's default test temp, on an input containing the fixes, passes the rust-tests stage.
